name: Mieming
kurzbeschreibung: Sprawling village scattered across the sunny Mieminger Plateau, offering views of the Tschirgant mountain range.
text:
Overview

Mieming is situated on the expansive Mieming Plateau, at an elevation of 864 meters, about 35 kilometers west of Innsbruck in the Imst district of Tyrol. Home to around 3,900 residents, Mieming is the largest community on the plateau and comprises several charming hamlets including Barwies, Obermieming, Untermieming, Fiecht, and See. Due to its exceptionally high count of annual sunshine hours, the area is famously known as the 'Sun Plateau'. The landscape is characterized by open larch meadows that turn brilliant gold in autumn, framed to the north by the majestic rock faces of the Mieming Range and the iconic Hohe Munde peak (2,662 m). Mieming successfully blends sophisticated Alpine hospitality, premium sporting facilities, and genuine village life into a top-tier holiday destination.

History

Human habitation on this sun-drenched plateau dates back to prehistory, confirmed by burial grounds from the Bronze and Hallstatt periods. The earliest written documentation appears in 1071 under the name 'Miemingen', referencing a Bavarian tribal settlement led by a clan elder named Miemo. For centuries, the plateau served as a crucial breadbasket for the Inn valley while offering a flood-safe travel route above the marshy river plains. The spiritual heart of the municipality is the parish church of the Assumption (Mariä Himmelfahrt) in Untermieming, featuring late Gothic foundations and elegant Baroque interior elements. In Obermieming, the Romanesque St. George's Church (Georgskirche) stands as one of Tyrol's oldest chapels, dating to the 11th century. Global fame arrived in the 1990s when Obermieming became the primary filming location for the hit European television series 'Der Bergdoktor'; the historic doctor's house remains a beloved local landmark.

Getting There

Mieming enjoys convenient access via high-capacity regional transport routes. By car, drivers take the A12 Inntal Autobahn to exit Telfs-West (coming from Innsbruck and the east) or exit Mötz (coming from the west), joining the B189 Mieminger federal road across the plateau. Travelers from Germany can arrive toll-free via Garmisch-Partenkirchen or the Fern Pass via Nassereith. By train, the nearest key stations are Telfs-Pfaffenhofen and Ötztal-Bahnhof. Frequent regional buses run every half hour from these rail hubs directly onto the Mieming Plateau, serving all hamlets and making car-free travel exceptionally easy and sustainable.

Tips

A flagship attraction is Golfpark Mieminger Plateau, recognized as one of the most scenic golf resorts in the Alps, offering an 18-hole championship course alongside a scenic 9-hole park course. In summer, the natural Badesee Mieming swimming lake in the hamlet of See provides crystal-clear water, manicured sunbathing lawns, and lakeside leisure for the whole family. Hikers should not miss the 'Larchsteig' educational path through the protected larch meadows, which create a golden wonderland every October. More adventurous trekkers can summit the Hohe Munde or hike to the rustic Alplhütte. TV drama enthusiasts will love strolling past the iconic Bergdoktorhaus in Obermieming during a relaxing village walk.
